title: Terms from the Tseitin clause chain
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, and let a literal on $n$ coordinates specify a coordinate and a required sign. Given two lists of such literals, assume that the coordinates within each list are pairwise distinct and that the two lists use disjoint coordinates. The Tseitin clause-chain construction applied to these lists yields clauses with pairwise distinct coordinates; regard each clause as a disjunctive-normal-form term by taking its literals and their coordinate list.
hypotheses_covered: The first list has pairwise distinct coordinate indices
The second list has pairwise distinct coordinate indices
The two lists have disjoint coordinate indices
caveat: The supplied statement refers to the Tseitin clause-chain construction but does not define it, so its output clauses cannot be described more explicitly.
